There is no tempting opposite reading, because nothing in the text concerns participation at all.

It merely allocates money.

opus.w: This is only the opening clause of an appropriations act. It sets aside Treasury funds to cover shortfalls for fiscal year 1947. No outside party (state, tribe, expert, company or member of the public) is consulted or brought into any federal decision. The general phrase 'for other purposes' does not create any participation process.
opus.b:
1. **Tempting-but-wrong reading:** None really applies. This is the standard opening clause of a deficiency appropriations act. Words like "supply deficiencies" and "for other purposes" don't describe any process that brings outside parties into a decision. No consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue appears, so nothing crosses the federal boundary.
